span.label: the first analysis of higher-order global statistical image properties of print advertisements, showing that man-made visually pleasing images share specific higher-order properties that distinguish them from other image types

span.label: The human visual system is adapted to process natural-scene statistics efficiently, so visually pleasing images that follow universal regularities can be processed efficiently.
span.term: efficient visual processing of natural-scene statistics
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: It has been proposed that stimuli which can be processed fluently are more aesthetic in general.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Higher-order image features may be processed fast at a lower level of the visual system, similar to gist perception of scenes, possibly before advertisement content is recognised.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Advertisements can activate the brain's reward circuitry, which is also involved in the perception of other visually pleasing images such as artworks.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Berlyne's u-shaped dependence of hedonic value on complexity was explained by the differing activation of two antagonistic brain systems, a reward system and an aversion system.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Humans may prefer fractal, self-similar geometry in architecture and urban scenes, possibly because ancestral natural surroundings had fractal characteristics.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Higher anisotropy in advertisements may arise from vertical text and image divisions along cardinal (horizontal and vertical) orientations.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Whether these image properties are necessary or sufficient to induce aesthetic perception, and how they correlate with brain activation, remains to be investigated.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The measured properties are not independent, so the precise relation between the different measures remains to be determined.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The dependence of beauty on complexity is not straightforward, and there is a general lack of well-controlled studies that manipulate complexity in such images.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Monochrome artworks are not equivalent to grayscale versions of colored paintings, because conversion to grayscale may destroy their aesthetic appeal.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The role of anisotropy in architectural aesthetics remains unclear.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Whether the specific pattern of the three measures is required or sufficient for aesthetic perception remains to be studied.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: higher-order image properties → aesthetic perception
span.note: The paper speculates that specific higher-order image properties may enhance visual effectiveness and play a causative role in judging stimuli pleasing, but whether they do remains to be investigated.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: processing fluency → aesthetic value
span.note: Stimuli that can be processed fluently are proposed to be more aesthetic in general.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: complexity → fractal dimension
span.note: Complexity and the fractal dimension are the most strongly correlated of the measures studied.

span.label: self-similarity → complexity
span.note: Self-similarity and complexity are also relatively strongly correlated across all images.

span.label: complexity - measured sense: the mean of all gradient strengths in the gradient image, an objective image statistic
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: complexity - hedonic/conceptual sense: Berlyne's information content, whose intermediate level is judged more aesthetic
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: complexity - fractal-dimension sense: the density of edges in a binarized image
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: self-similarity - measured sense: PHOG histogram-intersection similarity of image sections to a reference section across pyramid levels
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: self-similarity - fractal/aesthetic sense: fractal-like self-similar structure that can evoke aesthetic experience
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: anisotropy - measured sense: statistical variance of image-feature strength across orientations, distinguishing artworks (low) from advertisements (higher)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: aesthetic value - Birkhoff sense: a function of the ratio of order (here self-similarity) to complexity
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: aesthetics - computational sense: statistical image properties relatable to visual perception, as against the perceptual experience of pleasingness
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → the computational/statistical-image-properties approach to visual aesthetics (Redies, Amirshahi, Graham and colleagues)
span.note: Applies previously developed PHOG measures and Fourier/fractal analyses to advertisements and architecture.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → prior PHOG analyses that distinguish artworks from other image categories
span.note: Adds advertisements and architecture to the categories distinguished by the PHOG measures.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: supports → the idea that visually pleasing man-made images share specific higher-order statistical properties allowing efficient visual processing
span.note: Speculative extension of the idea to print advertising.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: supports → the biophilia hypothesis that humans prefer fractal, self-similar geometry in architecture
span.note: Self-similarity and complexity similarities support it, but anisotropy is much higher than in natural scenes.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: qualifies → Berlyne's link between intermediate complexity and aesthetic preference
span.note: Support is qualified by the lack of well-controlled complexity-manipulation studies.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On average, images of advertisements and artworks share a similar degree of complexity (fractal dimension) and self-similarity and similarities in the Fourier spectrum, but advertisements are more anisotropic than artworks.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Images of advertisements are characterized by a specific combination of higher-order image properties: high self-similarity, intermediate complexity and intermediate anisotropy.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: For single-product advertisements, the measured image properties do not depend on the type of product promoted (cars, cosmetics, fashion or other).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Median anisotropy is higher for advertisements than for artworks and natural scenes, and nearly all categories are significantly more anisotropic than artworks except the natural categories.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The measured properties are not independent; the strongest correlation is between complexity and the fractal dimension.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The PHOG measures (self-similarity, complexity and anisotropy) allow distinguishing artworks from many other image categories on average.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Statistical testing showed overall differences between all 15 image groups on all six measures (p < 0.001).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Images of architecture share statistical properties with images of advertisements to a large extent.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The three PHOG approaches to self-similarity (parent, neighbor, ground) give different absolute values but are robust for the relative differences between image categories.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
